\newcommand{\DhLargeDNote}{Additional runs for $L = 44$, $48$ and $56$ at diffusivities up to $5.8$ (Supplementary Material) show this high-diffusivity branch: beyond the sweep the participation ratio falls to a minimum of $0.79$, $0.74$ and $0.64$ near $D_I \approx 1.0$ and then rises towards one, crossing $0.9$ at $D_I \approx 1.3$, $1.4$ and $1.5$ (values interpolated on the grid of diffusivities). At these diffusivities much less infected mass is produced than inside the sweep ($M_I(T) \le 1.4$, against at least $5.7$ at $D_I = 0.72$), the coverage at the horizon is zero, and the crossing depends only weakly on $L$. This return to uniformity at large diffusivity lies outside the range described by \eqref{eq:Dh}, and we have not analysed it further. Repeating the two runs that bracket the crossing at $L = 44$ with half the time step, and with half the grid spacing and a quarter of the time step, changes $\mathrm{PR}(T)$ by at most $0.004$, the infected mass by at most $3.9\%$ (the coarse grid resolves the seed with about three cells per radius) and the interpolated crossing by at most $0.3\%$.}
\newcommand{\DhLargeDLetter}{In 18 additional runs for L = 44, 48 and 56 at diffusivities up to 5.8 the participation ratio falls to a minimum near a diffusivity of 1.0 and then rises towards one, crossing 0.9 at about 1.3, 1.4 and 1.5; much less infected mass is produced there than inside the sweep and the coverage at the horizon is zero. This return to uniformity at large diffusivity lies outside the range described by the fit, and we have not analysed it further.}
